Create a DETAILED infographic that acts as a “one-page map” of the sources.

Audience: [e.g., smart non-expert / new team member / exec].
Title: “[TOPIC]: One-Page Map”
Style: clean, professional, high-contrast, minimal clutter, icon-driven.

Layout (use clear labeled panels):
1) What this is (1 sentence) + Why it matters (3 bullets).
2) Key concepts (8–12 terms, each 6–10 words max).
3) The big picture (3–5 core themes that repeat across sources).
4) How it works (a 6–8 step flowchart with arrows).
5) Key evidence / key numbers (5–10 data points with units + short context).
6) Trade-offs (pros/cons or a 2x2 matrix with short labels).
7) Risks & failure modes (5–8, phrased as “If X, then Y”).
8) “What to read first” (recommended sequence of sections/sources for a beginner).
9) Glossary strip (5–10 tricky terms with ultra-short definitions).

Rules:
- Avoid paragraphs. Keep each block scannable.
- If sources disagree, label “Disputed” and show both sides briefly.
